justification: Formed a fresh view before opening prior rounds. The two pages re-fetched this round confirm last round's finding: neither has a real output panel for more than one snippet, neither has a theme-aware diagram pair, neither has runnable/verified code, and neither goes near dispatch mechanics. This page pairs every program with a real output panel (or a red does-not-compile/throws badge), has two SVG figures that are legible at 390px in both themes (checked fold-through on mobile-dark, spot-checked on desktop-dark and mobile-light), a two-column summary table that fits a phone with no scroll, five exercises spread through the article with collapsed solutions that give nothing away, three earned callouts, and a 17-item source list with inline numbered citations. Reading rhythm is short paragraphs punctuated by code, a numbered '4 design decisions' list, and a labelled figure — no walls of text on any device. I checked every round-1/round-2 blocker and major first: there were none outstanding (both rounds only ever carried minors past round 1, and round 1's single major — phone clipping of operative tokens — was marked fixed in round 2 and I confirm it stays fixed: I found no line in any mobile-dark screenshot where prose-critical code or a string literal is cut by the fade). Of round 2's six minors, four are now fixed: the code-highlighting drop on the PromoPlan block colors correctly throughout (desktop-light part 11, mobile-dark part 17); Figure 1's 'Invoice' label now sits clear of the arrowheads on its own line at the top-left of the box; the eight lines with fading trailing punctuation are gone (I could not find one at 41+ columns in the full mobile-dark or mobile-light pass); and both long listings (Invoice, plans) now have a `// --- the class ---` comment banner plus a lead-in sentence telling the phone reader which methods to read, so the block is no longer landmark-free. Two minors are unresolved and I am carrying them forward rather than inflating the score for effort spent elsewhere: the 'How do the four fit together?' synthesis paragraph still names `Compute`, a member that exists only inside Exercise 3's collapsed solution, so a reader who has not opened that solution meets an undefined name in the section meant to tie the whole article together; and the front matter still says `level: beginner` / `prerequisites: []` on a page whose second half covers method tables, guarded devirtualization and virtual stub dispatch, with nothing at the top of that half telling a beginner it is skippable (there is a skip-ahead sentence only at the very start of the runtime section, not reinforced by the badge). Neither blocks a pass on its own and neither is new; I list them because they still hold. Not a 10: those two nits, plus the still-open low-priority integrator note about desktop code column width, keep this short of 'clearly better with nothing left to point at'. It is comfortably past 8.5 (MDN/Real-Python quality with only nits) given the depth, verification and device coverage the compared pages simply do not have.
